newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Western investors scent Romania market prospects.
newsitem.headline: Western investors scent Romania market prospects.

text.p: A group of Western businessmen and bankers are in Romania to look into investment opportunities in the ex-communist country, the government said on Monday.

Representatives of 28 U.S. and European banks and firms, including Union Bank of Switzerland, Daiwa Europe Ltd and Morgan Stanley Asset Management, met Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea on a trip to assess Romania's economic potential, a government statement said.
Ciorbea said the visit was a "sign of support by western business and financial circles for reforms in Romania".

Romania is ruled by a centrist coalition which ousted leftists in last November's elections. The new government has pledged to step up free-market reforms and give increased incentives to foreign investors.
Direct foreign investment in Romania since the 1989 fall of communism stood at a little over $2 billion at end-1996, a level far below the foreign capital injections elsewhere in Eastern Europe.
